reading.title: Building effective agents
reading.why: Start with the simplest workflow that works and add agent complexity only when it measurably helps: the same discipline that keeps a two-week proof of concept scoped and demoable.

reading.title: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency
reading.why: Classic (2017) and still the reference for idempotency keys and retry with backoff and jitter, the exact habits needed when integrating with a customer's API; no newer first-party write-up replaces it.

reading.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
reading.why: Classic (2019) by Marc Brooker: why unbounded retries turn a slow customer API into an outage, and how capped backoff with jitter prevents it.

reading.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
reading.why: How to build, grade and maintain automated tests for agents so regressions show up before the customer sees them; maps to building the eval set and choosing code, model and human graders.

reading.title: Creating custom LLM judges to improve AI agent accuracy
reading.why: A vendor that deploys AI for enterprises shows judges tuned with expert feedback and checked against human raters: the practical way to trust a model grader.

reading.title: Beyond permission prompts: making Claude Code more secure and autonomous
reading.why: Filesystem and network isolation with an egress proxy and credentials kept outside the sandbox: the same ideas as least privilege and a restricted-network deployment.

reading.title: Incident report: Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025
reading.why: A timestamped public post-incident write-up (cause, detection, mitigation, restore): a model for runbooks, incident communication and the customer-facing report after a failure.

reading.title: Prompt caching with Claude
reading.why: Numbers for cutting cost by up to 90% and latency by up to 85% on long prompts, the lever behind unit economics for a customer deployment.

reading.title: Online migrations at scale
reading.why: Classic (2017): dual writes, backfill and live comparison to move data without downtime, the pattern behind zero-downtime migrations on a customer system; no newer first-party equivalent found.
